messages:
Tom Becker: opened PR to clarify the error-ref section around 429 vs timeouts and to add migration notes for SDK v1 -> v2. Found two stale links and one ambiguous example that mixes client-side timeouts with server 429 semantics. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/10042
Reba Singh: good catch. can you include a Go snippet? a few infra teams use Go clients and had trouble parsing Retry-After header ints vs floats.
Tom Becker: yes — I'll add a concise Go example and a small decision matrix. Also will note that Dedicated returns capacity-limited 429s with different headers (X-Capacity-Window) in some cases.
Ethan Cho: nit: we should show a curl that distinguishes client timeout from server 429 (use --max-time). Otherwise readers assume 429 == client timeout. quick repro:
Ethan Cho: ```bash
# server 429 test (delayed processing)
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-medium-1","input":"long prompt..."}'
# client timeout test (force client to cut)
curl --max-time 5 -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses ...
```
Marta Ruiz: adding an ops note would be great: Dedicated pools can return a 429 with X-Capacity-Window that indicates a short cooldown. Worth telling customers to prefer model fallback (smaller instance) in those cases.
docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/10042  build queued
Reba Singh: pushed a Go snippet in branch showing parsing Retry-After and fallback logic. here's the compact example I added: 
Reba Singh: ```go
// pseudo-code Go client (v2-like)
resp, err := client.Responses.Stream(ctx, &Request{Model:"rwd-medium-1", Input: TrimTail(prompt, 2048)})
if err != nil {
  if httpErr, ok := err.(HTTPError); ok && httpErr.StatusCode == 429 {
    retryAfter := parseRetryAfter(httpErr.Headers.Get("Retry-After"))
    if retryAfter > 0 {
      time.Sleep(time.Duration(retryAfter) * time.Second)
      // decide: rejoin (if resumable/idempotent) or fallback
    } else {
      // immediate fallback: trim prompt or switch model variant
    }
  }
}
```
Tom Becker: nice. I also added a tiny migration note: SDK v1 used `Retry-After` as string seconds while v2 normalizes header parsing and surfaces `retry_after_seconds` in error metadata. Call that out so teams migrating don't break backoff logic.
Ethan Cho: ran both curl tests in staging: confirmed server-side 429 flows differ from client socket timeouts. added a short line in the doc: "If you see an empty response + client-level timeout, investigate client-side timeout first before attempting retries."
Reba Singh: fixed the two stale links and updated the anchor to `#429-timeout-vs-client-timeout` to avoid future collisions. CI linted the new sample file for markdown length; trimmed comments and re-ran.
Marta Ruiz: added the small ops blurb about Dedicated 429 header differences and suggested a fallback order: 1) check Retry-After/X-Capacity-Window 2) trim prompt 3) smaller model variant 4) retry.
Tom Becker: CI passed :white_check_mark:. I'll merge and add a one-line release note: "Docs: clarified 429 vs client timeouts, added Go + curl snippets, migration note for SDK v2 header normalization."
docs-bot: PR merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/10042
Tom Becker: closing thread.
